name: DCM Pacific 1985: Red Tide
seed: Bungalow's Dynamic Campaign Pacific 1985: Red Tide
description:
4 May 1985, 0000 Zulu. For three weeks the Pacific Fleet has been at sea on manoeuvres, and the Americans have watched it as they always do, without alarm. Tonight the manoeuvres end. Within the hour the first missiles will fall on Kadena and Ching Chuan Kang; by first light Chinese landing ships will be on the beaches of southern Taiwan.

The plan was drawn in Moscow and in Beijing together, and it is simple. Strike while the enemy sleeps. Take Taiwan, then Okinawa, then Korea, then the Philippines, and last the straits of the south, before America can bring its strength across the Pacific. The Seventh Fleet is in harbour: Midway alongside at Yokosuka, Constellation at Subic Bay, the Marines' ships at White Beach. Our submarines already lie across the lanes from Pearl Harbor, and the missile submarines are safe in the Sea of Okhotsk.

The landing forces are loaded and at sea. The South Sea Fleet's landing squadron, with the 1st Marine Brigade aboard, is a few hours off Tsoying; the Pacific Fleet Landing Group, with the 55th Naval Infantry and Minsk's group around it, is two days from Okinawa.

You command the combined fleets in the Pacific. Take the islands, cut the sea lanes, and break the carriers when they come. The war ends when our flag flies over every base outside Australia and Hawaii, or when theirs flies over everything we hold beyond the Russian and Chinese mainland.

texts.guideWar: 4 May 1985, H-hour. The Soviet Union and China strike first, without warning: Taiwan, Okinawa, South Korea, the Philippines and the straits of the south are to be taken before America can reinforce across the Pacific. You command the combined fleets: the Soviet Pacific Fleet with its Cam Ranh squadron, and the PLA Navy's North, East and South Sea Fleets.
texts.guideWarTask: Two landing forces are already at sea and loaded: the South Sea Fleet's for Tsoying, a few hours out, and the Pacific Fleet's for White Beach on Okinawa, two days out. Your first task is to put them ashore; then take the rest of the island chain, and hold it against the American counter-stroke.
texts.guideHour2: At once the Main Naval Staff's war plan orders you to take Tsoying: ACCEPT it (the briefing opens by itself; with a panel open, the badge on the Admiralty icon shows it waiting). The next orders of the plan follow as each target falls.
texts.guideHour3: Select the South Sea Fleet Landing Squadron off southern Taiwan (click it on the map, or in the Formation Manager): 8 battalions aboard, its escort around it.
texts.guideHour4: Right-click Tsoying and choose Invade. Its defences meet the group 50 nm out; within 20 nm it must destroy them all, then hold 4 hours. Strike Ching Chuan Kang from the air first.
texts.guideHour6: Press Space or Play (top right). When the defences or an enemy group are met, the contact screen comes up.
texts.guideExampleMove: The Missile Cruiser Brigade holds east of Honshu. Right-click the sea south of Yokosuka: it plots a sea route and shows its arrival time at each waypoint.
texts.guideExampleSplit: Split the Krivak Revnostny off the Pacific Fleet Landing Group to escort a convoy into White Beach once it is ours, then merge her back when the convoy is safely in.
texts.guideLift: Battalions ride in landing ships: Ivan Rogov, Ropucha, Alligator and the Chinese Yukan 2 each (the enemy's: Tarawa 3, Austin 2, Charleston or Newport 1).
texts.guideLiftIslands: Select the group and right-click an enemy port, or an island airfield with no port (Wake, Midway, Kwajalein).
texts.guideExampleInvade: The Pacific Fleet Landing Group carries 8 battalions (Ivan Rogov, Aleksandr Nikolayev, BDK-101 and BDK-98, 2 each): enough for a port such as White Beach, not for a depot such as Subic Bay, which needs 15.
texts.guideDeckRates: the Kiev and the Orel 8; the enemy's Midway 6, Forrestal, Kitty Hawk and America 8, Enterprise and Nimitz 10
texts.guideExampleCarrier: Minsk loses 4 Yak-38s and 2 Ka-27s over the Ryukyus: back at Vladivostok, Replace lost aircraft costs 15 % of those 6 aircraft's price. At Sovetskaya Gavan (no depot) she can refill her magazine from the base's aviation stores, as far as they go, but not replace aircraft.
texts.guideReplen: Your side starts with none. The Kazbek (fuel) and the Boris Chilikin (fuel and some weapons) are in the Shipyard panel, under Replenishment (their card says what each carries). In a friendly port they load from its stock, never taking it below half of what it should hold.
texts.guideTanker: Your side has no tanker aircraft: the game has no Soviet or Chinese tanker of 1985 (the enemy keeps a KC-10A Extender at NAF Atsugi). How a tanker works:
texts.guideExampleStrike: The four H-6Ds at Shanghai-Dachang with a Strike loadout on Ching Chuan Kang before the Tsoying landing: fewer fighters to meet your landing ships.
texts.guideDepots: Vladivostok, Shanghai, Cam Ranh Bay. They make fuel and weapons every day and send the convoys by themselves. Each makes its own share: lose one, and your side makes that much less.
texts.guideExampleSupply: Tsoying, once taken, is the next base to be fought for: set it to High so its missiles are topped up before the counter-attack comes.
texts.guideExampleIntel: "A satellite pass at 0456Z shows about 6 surface ships 140 nm from Yokosuka": the red circle on the map is that area, not a firm position.
texts.guideCarrierPrices: Their price in the Shipyard panel. Carriers by tier: Moskva 300, Kiev 750, Orel 1,300.
texts.guideYardsList: Ships join at your shipyards (the crane badge: Vladivostok, Shanghai, Cam Ranh Bay), aircraft at the airfield by them.
texts.guideVictory: The first side to hold every base in the theatre but those on the enemy's home soil wins: for you, everything outside mainland Australia and Hawaii (Pearl Harbor and Hickam), Japan, Guam and Port Moresby included; for the enemy, everything outside the Russian and Chinese mainland, islands included (Sakhalin, Hainan, Zhoushan...).
texts.guideRoad: Tsoying first (it brings Ching Chuan Kang with it), then White Beach and Kadena, then Chinhae; then Subic Bay (a depot: 15 battalions) with Clark, and last the south: Singapore, Malaya and the Indonesian ports. Then Japan.
texts.guideFieldModels: (the small field in its US, Japanese and Chinese versions, the US one under the allies' flags at Ching Chuan Kang, Tengah, Kuantan, Butterworth, Halim and Iswahjudi and under Australia's at its fields; the NATO airbase for the big US fields, Kadena, Clark, Misawa, Andersen and Hickam; for the Soviets' a Soviet field sized by the base, the small fighter field only where no large aircraft are based: one where a bomber or patrol aircraft is based stands as a larger one)
texts.guideReplenStart: Your side starts with none: order a Kazbek or a Boris Chilikin. The enemy's T2 oiler and Flint (Kilauea class) at Subic Bay and Sacramento at Pearl Harbor start loaded.
texts.guideAllies: (Soviet ships rearm in Chinese ports and the other way round, as the enemy's American ships do in Australian and allied ports)
texts.guideBatteries: (Soviet: Rubezh and Redut; China: HY-2 and HY-1; the enemy's US and Japanese bases M110 and M109 guns, Australia's M109, its allies' M110 or M109)
texts.guideSams: (Soviet: SA-3, SA-8; China: SA-2 for its HQ-2; the enemy's US: Nike Hercules; Japan: Nike Hercules, Type 81; Australia, Singapore and Indonesia: Rapier; Taiwan: Skyguard; Korea: Vulcan guns, Malaysia: M42 guns, in place of SAM sites)
texts.guideCaptured: The allied bases start light, at 30 % of their stocks (one battery); the US bases on Okinawa at 55 % (two). Clark AB starts at 55 % of its own stocks too, but it is one place with Subic Bay, a depot at full stocks: the two are defended together, with all four batteries.
texts.guideOpeningWarning: The war plan's orders come from the Main Naval Staff: Tsoying at once, White Beach a day in, Chinhae 4 days in, Subic Bay 10 and Singapore 20, each sooner once the one before it has fallen (they take no room from the others);
texts.guideEnemy: The enemy plays under the same fog, with its own sensors and reports. Its daily income is 1.5 times what its bases pay (Normal, the one difficulty for now; its bases pay more than yours: 128 a day against 76 at the start). It starts on a peacetime footing, 47 ships, nearly all in port: Midway's group at Yokosuka, Constellation's at Subic Bay, the amphibious group at White Beach, the Japanese escort flotillas in their home ports, the Australians at Fleet Base East; only two attack submarines are out, off Kamchatka and in the Sea of Japan, and one Japanese flotilla is meant to patrol west of Kyushu. Its allies' squadrons (Taiwanese, Philippine, Malaysian and Indonesian F-5s) fly for it from their own fields and are never replaced. Its orders arrive in half your time (in half that again while its warships are under half of what it may have, twice your ships), ships at Pearl Harbor, Yokosuka and Fleet Base East, aircraft at the fields by them. It never has more than twice your ships (its own on order counted, landing ships aside), at most 12 aircraft on order at once and never more than twice your aircraft, your carriers' counted, and below 20 escorts it gets escorts back at once, free, as far as twice your ships allow. It organises its fleet into capital groups, surface action groups, ASW and patrol groups and submarine groups; it keeps landing ships on each front, north and south of 25°N, and lands with 6 battalions or so, retaking its lost ports first and at once, then going for its objectives, weighing each target's sailing time against the defence it knows there. It raids your groups at sea with 2 to 8 anti-ship aircraft when one of its spotters holds them (a patrol aircraft, a ship or a submarine), escorted by fighters where they reach; strikes your airfields near its landings' targets and, now and then, the nearest where it knows your aircraft are; escorts its convoys once it loses them on a lane, blockades your ports with submarines, and keeps three fighter patrols of two up. None of its surface ships goes on a mission alone, and its carriers short of a third of their wing sail for a depot to replace their losses. It doesn't use its replenishment ships or its KC-10A.
texts.guideYards: The catalogue's tiers open with your rank (renown {ranks}); a ship's loadouts open by rank too. Ships take 5 to 20 days to arrive (the enemy's half that) and join at a shipyard: Vladivostok and Cam Ranh Bay for Soviet ships, Shanghai and Cam Ranh Bay for Chinese ones, the safest of them unless you pick one (the enemy's Pearl Harbor, Yokosuka and Fleet Base East; ships are ordered at these only); aircraft are delivered to the airfield by the first of their nation's yards (Knevichi for Soviet aircraft, Shanghai-Dachang for Chinese ones) unless you pick Cam Ranh Bay under Join at. The enemy's tier grows with the days of war. Prices are the game's own point values (a Krivak I 66, a Udaloy 387, a Slava 1,058, a Su-24M 88 each); carriers are priced by tier: Moskva 300, Kiev 750, Orel 1,300 (the enemy's Forrestal 1,250, Kitty Hawk and Enterprise 1,400, America 1,500, Nimitz 1,600), and they take longest to arrive: Moskva 14 days, Kiev 17, Orel 20 (Forrestal 16, Kitty Hawk and Enterprise 18, America 19, Nimitz 20), every other ship 5 to 15 by its price; replenishment ships: the Kazbek 100, the Boris Chilikin 150.
texts.guideVictoryDepth: Each side's objectives are every base but the enemy's home soil, marked in the campaign: the enemy's home soil is mainland Australia (HMAS Stirling included), which you need not take; yours is the Russian and Chinese mainland, which the enemy need not take. The first to hold all of its objectives has won; later changes don't undo it. Hawaii (Pearl Harbor and Hickam) is no objective for you, though the enemy must hold it.
texts.guideSamReach: Nike Hercules 70 nm, SA-2 and HQ-2 25, SA-3 15, SA-8 6, Type 81 5, Rapier 4, Skyguard 3
texts.guideColocated: Sokol AB with Korsakov, Lingshui AB with Yulin; the enemy's Misawa AB with Ominato, Clark AB with Subic Bay, RAAF Williamtown with Fleet Base East
texts.guideReplenShips: (the Boris Chilikin 13,000 t of fuel and 400 t of weapons, the Kazbek 10,000 t of fuel; the enemy's Sacramento 24,000 t of fuel and 2,150 t of weapons, T2 oiler 16,000 t of fuel, Kilauea 5,000 t of weapons)
texts.victorySummary: The campaign is won by the first side to hold every base in the theatre but those on the enemy's home soil. Islands count (Taiwan, Okinawa, Japan, Guam, Sakhalin, Hainan...), and each side must keep its own bases too. Hawaii is not an objective for us.
texts.endingWon: The last base the enemy held beyond Australia and Hawaii has fallen. The American fleet is back behind its own coasts, and the Western Pacific is ours. The war is won.
texts.endingLost: The enemy holds every base we had beyond the Russian and Chinese mainland. What is left of the fleets has fallen back to Vladivostok and the Chinese ports. The war is lost.
texts.procurementLift: a place in a landing ship (Ivan Rogov, Ropucha, Alligator and Yukan 2 each · the enemy's Tarawa 3, Austin 2, Charleston or Newport 1)
texts.messageVictory: Victory. Every base outside the enemy's home soil{besides} is ours: the campaign is won.
texts.messageDefeat: Defeat. {winner} holds every base outside our home soil{besides}: the campaign is lost.

situation: As of 0000Z the Soviet Union and the People's Republic of China are at war with the United States, Japan and their allies in the Pacific. No declaration has been made: the enemy has had no warning beyond what his own intelligence made of our exercises.

The war plan of the Main Naval Staff is now in force: Taiwan first, then Okinawa, then South Korea; then the Philippines, and last Singapore, Malaya and the Indonesian islands. Taken quickly, they give us the island chain and the straits before America can reinforce across the Pacific.
The north is the Pacific Fleet's, with the North and East Sea Fleets of the PLA Navy. The south is run from Cam Ranh Bay, where our squadron and the South Sea Fleet are to close the South China Sea.
Supply comes from Vladivostok, Shanghai and Cam Ranh Bay. Every port we take must be fed by convoy until it can feed the next landing.
enemy: The enemy is on a peacetime footing. The Seventh Fleet is in harbour: the carrier Midway at Yokosuka, Constellation at Subic Bay, the amphibious group at White Beach. The Japanese escort flotillas lie in their home ports. Expect him to wake quickly, and to answer first from the air, from Kadena, Misawa and Clark.
The allied garrisons on Taiwan, in Korea and in the south are light and short of stocks. The American bases on Okinawa and in the Philippines are better found.
Once roused, he will bring his carriers against our landings and run his convoys from Pearl Harbor under escort. His patrol aircraft will look for our submarines, his ships and submarines hunt them.
intent: Take Tsoying, then Okinawa. The landing forces are at sea and loaded: every hour the enemy has to prepare is against us.
Strike the enemy's airfields before each landing goes in, and keep the escorts close round the landing ships.
Our submarines across the Pacific are to attack enemy shipping and report every movement from Pearl Harbor and Guam. The missile submarines stay in the Okhotsk bastion.
Preserve the carriers, keep the convoys moving, and be ready for the American counter-stroke.
